hypothesis: There exists a system with a very short rule and a trivial initial condition whose behaviour is complex by standard operational measures: elementary rule 30 (an 8-bit rule) started from a single black cell produces a centre column that is not eventually periodic, is essentially incompressible, and passes standard randomness tests, and a space-time pattern that is far less compressible than those of nested or repetitive rules of the same description length.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Rule 30 from a single black cell on a lattice wide enough that boundaries never influence the measured cells. (a) Compressibility: the lzma-compressed size of the first 2^16 centre-column bits (packed 8 per byte) is at least 0.95 times the compressed size of 2^16 bits from os.urandom packed the same way. (b) Aperiodicity: no period p <= 2^15 holds from any offset t0 <= 2^15 within the first 2^16 centre-column bits (i.e. for every p there is a t >= 2^15 with x[t] != x[t+p]). (c) Randomness tests on the 2^16 centre-column bits: monobit frequency test p > 0.01, Wald-Wolfowitz runs test p > 0.01, chi-square test on the 256 frequencies of non-overlapping 8-bit blocks p > 0.01. (d) Pattern complexity relative to simple rules: the lzma ratio (compressed/raw bytes of the packed bit image) of the 1001-step single-cell pattern (rows of 2001 cells) is at least 5 times larger for rule 30 than for the nested rule 90 and at least 5 times larger than for the repetitive rule 250. 'Supports' requires (a)-(d). In addition the census of all 256 elementary rules by the same pattern ratio is reported (number of rules with ratio > 0.5 of rule 30's ratio), without bearing on the verdict.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' (for the witness, and hence failing to confirm the existence claim) if the rule-30 centre column is eventually periodic with period <= 2^15 within 2^16 steps, or if its lzma ratio is below 0.5 of the random baseline. Other combinations are 'mixed'.
interpretation: The claim is a general-principle existence statement ('can nevertheless show'); it is tested on its canonical witness, rule 30, as both assessors propose. 'Simple rule' = 8-bit rule table; 'simple initial condition' = one black cell. 'Highly complex behaviour' is operationalized as incompressibility (lzma), absence of periodicity, and passing standard randomness tests of the centre column, plus a comparison of pattern compressibility with nested (rule 90) and repetitive (rule 250) rules of identical description length. Rule numbering is Wolfram's. A single test battery is used; a sequence can be complex under these tests and simple under others (the assessors' obstacle), and the claim's 'general phenomenon' aspect is only illustrated by the census, not established.
